title: Recordings with Multiple Neuropixels Probes in Head-Restrained Mice
author: Susu Chen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8tphwmn

steps.title: Prepare Manipulators and Probes
steps.instruction: Set up the hardware and software configuration for the Neuropixels probes.

substeps.instruction: Set manipulator azimuth and pitch angles based on target brain regions to ensure target reach and avoid collisions.
Mount and fix individual probes onto manipulators.
Connect Neuropixels probe cables to headstages.
Connect individual reference cables to pins soldered onto each probe (note: ground and external reference pads are shorted together on the flex).
Connect all electrode reference cables to a common reference electrode.
Launch SpikeGLX software to verify probe detection.
Configure recording settings in SpikeGLX, including Imec Readout Table (imRo), trigger mode, and file save locations.

steps.title: Prepare Animal and Recording Well
steps.instruction: Immobilize the animal and prepare the brain surface for recording.

substeps.instruction: Load animal into recording apparatus and immobilize the head.
Remove dura seal (Kwik-cast sealant).
Fill the recording well with ~0.1 ml of cortex buffer.
Place the common reference electrode cable into the cortex buffer bath, ensuring it is far from any potential insertion craniotomy.
Rinse the well and reference electrode multiple times with cortex buffer to remove debris, then refill the well.

steps.title: Position and Penetrate Probes
steps.instruction: Carefully insert probes into the target brain regions.

substeps.instruction: Move probes above target craniotomies and identify clean entry points, avoiding surface blood vessels.
Ensure entry points from separate sessions are at least 200 μm apart if using the same penetration angle.
Fine-adjust the entry point using the micro-manipulator.
Move the probe along the penetration axis to assist dura penetration (probes should be sharpened before usage).
Maintain probe bending from base to tip at < 100 µm during insertion.
If dura penetration is difficult, bend the probe by less than 200 µm (manipulator reading) and gently tap the convex side with a gauge 28 fine syringe tip until penetration is achieved.
Slowly move the probe in and out until the first row of recording sites is at the brain surface (verified via high-power stereo microscope).
Ensure the tip of the shank (triangle region) is completely inside the brain, then zero the manipulator depth reading at the brain surface.
Penetrate probes through dura one at a time.
Drive all probes to targeted depths simultaneously using automatic stepping at a speed of approximately 6~8 µm/s (e.g., 3~4 µm/step, 1 step = 0.5 sec).
Record the final depths as the distance from the brain surface.

steps.title: Stabilize and Record
steps.instruction: Allow the brain to settle and maintain hydration during the recording session.

substeps.instruction: Wait 00:10:00 for the brain to settle after full insertion before starting recording.
Fill the recording well with at least 0.1 ml of cortex buffer to prevent brain surface drying during the 1~2 hour session.

steps.title: Post-Recording Retrieval and Sealing
steps.instruction: Remove probes and seal the craniotomies.

substeps.instruction: Retract probes using manipulators, either manually one at a time or via automated program.
Disconnect probes and reference cables.
Dismount probes and immerse the shank part (not the base) in cleaning solution at room temperature (RT) for 12:00:00.
Remove the common reference electrode from the recording well.
Rinse the well multiple times with cortex buffer.
Absorb all cortex buffer with a sugi sponge, ensuring the surface is moist but without excessive liquid.
Apply Kwik-cast sealant to cover all craniotomies.
Remove animal from the rig after Kwik-cast has solidified (~ 3 min).

steps.title: Probe Cleaning and Storage
steps.instruction: Perform final cleaning of probes before the next use.

substeps.instruction: Wash probes in distilled water for 02:00:00.
Perform a quick dip in IPA to remove DiI from previous penetration.
Allow cleaned probes to dry in air.
